notes: BATCH_001 General Awareness part: 150 original questions on the static GA topics (Government Schemes, Important Days, National and International Organizations, Important Reports and Indexes, Government Policies, Static Awareness). No current-affairs topics. Every question has web fact checks dated 2026-11-05; facts that can change carry current_affairs review dates. Pending human review.

questions.subject: General Awareness and Current Affairs
questions.question_text: Under the PM-KISAN scheme, how much income support does an eligible landholding farmer family receive in a year?

solution.explanation: PM-KISAN (Pradhan Mantri Kisan Samman Nidhi), launched on 24 February 2019 by the Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare, pays ₹6,000 a year in three equal instalments of ₹2,000 directly into Aadhaar-seeded bank accounts through DBT. It began for small and marginal farmers and was extended to all landholding farmers from 1 June 2019.
steps: Paid in three equal instalments of ₹2,000 by DBT
solution.final_answer: Option A: ₹6,000 in three equal instalments

fact_checks.claim: PM-KISAN launched 24 Feb 2019; ₹6,000 per year in three equal instalments by DBT; extended to all landholding farmers from 1 June 2019

questions.subject: General Awareness and Current Affairs
questions.question_text: On which date was the Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana (PMJDY) launched?

solution.explanation: PMJDY, the National Mission for Financial Inclusion, was launched by the Prime Minister on 28 August 2014. It gives every unbanked adult a basic savings account with a free RuPay debit card. The Department of Financial Services (Ministry of Finance) runs it.
solution.why_others_wrong: 15 August 2014 is the Independence Day speech in which it was announced; 2 October 2014 is the launch of Swachh Bharat Mission.

fact_checks.claim: PMJDY was launched by the Prime Minister on 28 August 2014

questions.subject: General Awareness and Current Affairs
questions.question_text: What is the annual premium payable by a subscriber under the Pradhan Mantri Suraksha Bima Yojana (PMSBY)?

solution.explanation: PMSBY is an accident insurance scheme for people aged 18 to 70 with a bank or post office account. For an annual premium of ₹20 (₹12 before 2022) it gives ₹2 lakh for accidental death or total permanent disability and ₹1 lakh for partial disability.
solution.why_others_wrong: ₹12 was the old PMSBY premium; ₹436 is the PMJJBY (life cover) premium; ₹330 was the old PMJJBY premium.

fact_checks.claim: PMSBY premium ₹20 a year (earlier ₹12); cover ₹2 lakh / ₹1 lakh; age 18-70

questions.subject: General Awareness and Current Affairs
questions.question_text: The Pradhan Mantri Ujjwala Yojana, which provides LPG connections to women of poor households, is implemented by which ministry?

options.text: Ministry of Women and Child Development
Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food and Public Distribution
Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas

solution.explanation: PMUY was launched by the Prime Minister at Ballia, Uttar Pradesh, on 1 May 2016 by the Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas. Its first target was 5 crore deposit-free LPG connections to BPL households in three years; the target was later raised to 8 crore.
steps: PMUY is a Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas scheme
Launched at Ballia, UP, on 1 May 2016
solution.final_answer: Option D: Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas

fact_checks.claim: PMUY launched at Ballia on 1 May 2016 by the Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas; 5 crore BPL connections in three years

questions.subject: General Awareness and Current Affairs
questions.question_text: Under Ayushman Bharat Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana (AB PM-JAY), what is the health cover per family per year?

solution.explanation: AB PM-JAY gives each eligible family cover of up to ₹5 lakh a year for secondary and tertiary care hospitalisation, cashless, at empanelled public and private hospitals. It is run by the National Health Authority.
steps: PM-JAY cover: ₹5,00,000 per family per year

fact_checks.claim: PM-JAY provides coverage up to ₹5,00,000 per family per year for secondary and tertiary care hospitalisation

questions.subject: General Awareness and Current Affairs
questions.question_text: The PM SVANidhi scheme provides collateral-free working capital loans to which group?

solution.explanation: PM SVANidhi (PM Street Vendor's AtmaNirbhar Nidhi) was launched by the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs on 1 June 2020 to help street vendors restart businesses hit by COVID-19, through collateral-free working capital loans in rising tranches, an interest subsidy and cashback for digital payments.
solution.why_others_wrong: Traditional artisans are covered by PM Vishwakarma; farmers by PM-KISAN.

fact_checks.claim: PM SVANidhi launched by MoHUA on 1 June 2020 to give street vendors collateral-free working capital loans

questions.subject: General Awareness and Current Affairs
questions.question_text: Which ministry implements the SVAMITVA scheme, under which drones are used to map rural inhabited land and issue property cards?

options.text: Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs

solution.explanation: SVAMITVA (Survey of Villages and Mapping with Improvised Technology in Village Areas) was launched by the Prime Minister on National Panchayati Raj Day, 24 April 2020. The Ministry of Panchayati Raj implements it with the Survey of India; owners get a 'record of rights' (property card) that can be used for bank loans.
steps: SVAMITVA is a Ministry of Panchayati Raj scheme
Launched on National Panchayati Raj Day, 24 April 2020
solution.final_answer: Option D: Ministry of Panchayati Raj

fact_checks.claim: SVAMITVA launched on 24 April 2020; Ministry of Panchayati Raj with Survey of India; drone survey and property cards

questions.subject: General Awareness and Current Affairs
questions.question_text: Jal Jeevan Mission, which aims to give every rural household a functional household tap connection, is implemented by which ministry?

options.text: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs

solution.explanation: Jal Jeevan Mission is run by the Ministry of Jal Shakti in partnership with the States. Its goal is a Functional Household Tap Connection (FHTC) for every rural home.
steps: JJM: tap water to every rural household
solution.final_answer: Option A: Ministry of Jal Shakti

fact_checks.claim: Jal Jeevan Mission is run by the Ministry of Jal Shakti with States to provide FHTCs to rural households

questions.subject: General Awareness and Current Affairs
questions.question_text: PM Vishwakarma scheme supports artisans and craftspeople working in how many traditional trades?

solution.explanation: PM Vishwakarma, run mainly by the Ministry of MSME, supports artisans in 18 family-based traditional trades such as carpenter, boat maker, goldsmith, potter, barber, tailor and fishing-net maker. It gives recognition (a certificate and ID card), skill training, a toolkit incentive, collateral-free credit and digital incentives.

fact_checks.claim: PM Vishwakarma covers 18 family-based traditional trades; Ministry of MSME

questions.subject: General Awareness and Current Affairs
questions.question_text: The Soil Health Card scheme was launched by the Prime Minister on 19 February 2015 at which place?

solution.explanation: The Soil Health Card scheme was launched at Suratgarh, Rajasthan, on 19 February 2015. Each card reports the soil's nutrient status and recommends fertiliser doses. Since 2022-23 it is the 'Soil Health & Fertility' component of the Rashtriya Krishi Vikas Yojana.
solution.why_others_wrong: Panipat: Beti Bachao Beti Padhao (2015); Ballia: Ujjwala (2016); Ranchi: PM-JAY (2018).

fact_checks.claim: PM launched the Soil Health Card scheme on 19 February 2015 at Suratgarh, Rajasthan

questions.subject: General Awareness and Current Affairs
questions.question_text: Up to what age of a girl child can a Sukanya Samriddhi Yojana account be opened in her name?

solution.explanation: A Sukanya Samriddhi account can be opened from the birth of a girl child until she turns 10. The minimum deposit is ₹250 and the maximum ₹1.5 lakh a year; the account matures 21 years after opening. SSY was launched on 22 January 2015 under Beti Bachao, Beti Padhao.

fact_checks.claim: SSY account can be opened from birth until the girl attains 10 years; matures after 21 years; ₹250 minimum, ₹1.5 lakh maximum a year

questions.subject: General Awareness and Current Affairs
questions.question_text: In which year was the 'Make in India' initiative launched?

solution.explanation: Make in India was launched on 25 September 2014 to make India a global manufacturing hub. Its current phase, Make in India 2.0, focuses on 27 sectors.

fact_checks.claim: Make in India was launched on 25 September 2014

questions.subject: General Awareness and Current Affairs
questions.question_text: What is the entry age group for the Pradhan Mantri Jeevan Jyoti Bima Yojana (PMJJBY)?

solution.explanation: PMJJBY is a one-year renewable life cover of ₹2 lakh for death from any cause, for a premium of ₹436 a year. It is open to bank or post office account holders aged 18 to 50; those who join before 50 can keep the cover up to 55 by paying the premium.
solution.why_others_wrong: 18-40 is the Atal Pension Yojana entry age; 18-70 is PMSBY.

fact_checks.claim: PMJJBY: ₹2 lakh life cover, ₹436 premium, age 18-50

questions.subject: General Awareness and Current Affairs
questions.question_text: Atal Pension Yojana (APY) guarantees a monthly pension in which range after the subscriber turns 60?

solution.explanation: APY is open to bank account holders aged 18 to 40 who are not income-tax payers. Depending on the contribution and the entry age, it guarantees a monthly pension of ₹1,000, 2,000, 3,000, 4,000 or 5,000 from age 60.
solution.why_others_wrong: ₹3,000 fixed is the PM Shram Yogi Maan-dhan and PM Kisan Maan-dhan pension.

fact_checks.claim: APY: age 18-40, non-income-tax payers, guaranteed pension ₹1,000 to ₹5,000 a month after 60

questions.subject: General Awareness and Current Affairs
questions.question_text: Under the Pradhan Mantri MUDRA Yojana, what is the upper loan limit of the 'Tarun Plus' category introduced in 2024?

solution.explanation: PMMY (launched 8 April 2015) gives collateral-free loans to non-farm micro enterprises in categories Shishu (up to ₹50,000), Kishore (₹50,000 to ₹5 lakh) and Tarun (₹5 lakh to ₹10 lakh). Tarun Plus, announced in the Union Budget 2024-25 and effective 24 October 2024, covers ₹10 lakh to ₹20 lakh for borrowers who have repaid an earlier Tarun loan.

fact_checks.claim: MUDRA loan limit raised to ₹20 lakh from ₹10 lakh through the Tarun Plus category
PMMY launched 8 April 2015

questions.subject: General Awareness and Current Affairs
questions.question_text: Stand-Up India facilitates bank loans in which range for SC/ST and women entrepreneurs setting up greenfield enterprises?

solution.explanation: Stand-Up India (launched 5 April 2016) facilitates bank loans between ₹10 lakh and ₹1 crore to at least one SC or ST borrower and at least one woman borrower per bank branch, for a greenfield enterprise. Borrowers must be above 18 years.
steps: Stand-Up India range: ₹10 lakh to ₹1 crore
At least one SC/ST and one woman borrower per branch
solution.why_others_wrong: Up to ₹20 lakh is the MUDRA Tarun Plus ceiling.

fact_checks.claim: Stand-Up India facilitates bank loans between ₹10 lakh and ₹1 crore to SC/ST and women entrepreneurs; at least one of each per bank branch

questions.subject: General Awareness and Current Affairs
questions.question_text: What concessional rate of interest does a beneficiary pay on the collateral-free enterprise development loan under PM Vishwakarma?

solution.explanation: PM Vishwakarma gives collateral-free loans of ₹1 lakh (first tranche, 18 months) and ₹2 lakh (second tranche, 30 months). The beneficiary pays a concessional 5%; the Ministry of MSME pays interest subvention capped at 8%, and the Government bears the credit guarantee fee. The scheme was launched on Vishwakarma Jayanti, 17 September 2023.
steps: Subvention up to 8% paid by MoMSME
solution.why_others_wrong: 8% is the cap on the interest subvention the government pays to the lender, not the borrower's rate.

fact_checks.claim: Concessional interest 5% charged from the beneficiary; interest subvention cap of 8% paid by MoMSME; ₹1 lakh and ₹2 lakh tranches
PM Vishwakarma launched on Vishwakarma Jayanti, 17 September 2023

questions.subject: General Awareness and Current Affairs
questions.question_text: Under the Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana, what is the maximum premium payable by farmers for Rabi food and oilseed crops?

solution.explanation: PMFBY (approved January 2016, from Kharif 2016) caps the farmer's premium at 2% for Kharif food and oilseed crops, 1.5% for Rabi food and oilseed crops and 5% for annual commercial and horticultural crops. The rest of the premium is paid by the Centre and States. It replaced NAIS and MNAIS.

fact_checks.claim: PMFBY farmer premium: 2% Kharif, 1.5% Rabi, 5% annual commercial/horticultural crops

questions.subject: General Awareness and Current Affairs
questions.question_text: PM-Surya Ghar: Muft Bijli Yojana, approved by the Union Cabinet in February 2024, aims to install rooftop solar in how many households?

solution.explanation: The Cabinet approved PM-Surya Ghar: Muft Bijli Yojana on 29 February 2024 with an outlay of ₹75,021 crore to install rooftop solar in one crore households, which are expected to get up to 300 units of free electricity a month. The Ministry of New and Renewable Energy runs it.
steps: Benefit: up to 300 units a month

fact_checks.claim: Cabinet approved PM-Surya Ghar on 29 Feb 2024, ₹75,021 crore, rooftop solar for one crore households, up to 300 units free a month

questions.subject: General Awareness and Current Affairs
questions.question_text: Under the Pradhan Mantri Garib Kalyan Anna Yojana as extended from 1 January 2024, how much free foodgrain does an Antyodaya Anna Yojana (AAY) household get each month?

solution.explanation: In November 2023 the Cabinet decided to give free foodgrains under PMGKAY to about 81.35 crore beneficiaries for five years from 1 January 2024: 35 kg per AAY household per month and 5 kg per person per month for Priority Households, as entitled under the National Food Security Act.
steps: AAY: 35 kg per household per month
Priority household: 5 kg per person per month
solution.why_others_wrong: 5 kg is the per-person entitlement of priority households.

fact_checks.claim: Free foodgrains for 81.35 crore for five years from 1 Jan 2024; 35 kg per AAY household, 5 kg per person for PHH

questions.subject: General Awareness and Current Affairs
questions.question_text: The Pradhan Mantri Shram Yogi Maan-dhan (PM-SYM) pension scheme is meant for unorganised workers with a monthly income of up to how much?

solution.explanation: PM-SYM (launched in 2019) is a voluntary, contributory pension scheme for unorganised workers aged 18 to 40 with a monthly income of up to ₹15,000. The worker's contribution (₹55 to ₹200 a month by entry age) is matched by the government, and a minimum pension of ₹3,000 a month is paid from age 60.
solution.why_others_wrong: ₹21,000 is the ESI wage ceiling.

fact_checks.claim: PM-SYM for unorganised workers with monthly income up to ₹15,000, age 18-40, ₹3,000 pension

questions.subject: General Awareness and Current Affairs
questions.question_text: Which institution is the pension fund manager of the Pradhan Mantri Kisan Maan-Dhan Yojana (PM-KMY)?

options.text: Pension Fund Regulatory and Development Authority

solution.explanation: PM-KMY is a voluntary contributory pension scheme for small and marginal farmers aged 18 to 40. It pays a minimum pension of ₹3,000 a month after 60; the Centre matches the farmer's contribution 1:1. LIC is the pension fund manager and handles the pension payout.
solution.why_others_wrong: PFRDA regulates the NPS and APY; it is not the fund manager of PM-KMY.
solution.final_answer: Option D: Life Insurance Corporation of India

fact_checks.claim: LIC shall be the Pension Fund Manager and responsible for pension payout under PM-KMY; age 18-40; ₹3,000

questions.subject: General Awareness and Current Affairs
questions.question_text: The first flight under the UDAN regional connectivity scheme, flagged off by the Prime Minister on 27 April 2017, connected Delhi with which city?

solution.explanation: UDAN (Ude Desh ka Aam Nagrik) was launched on 21 October 2016 by the Ministry of Civil Aviation under the National Civil Aviation Policy 2016 to connect unserved and underserved airports. The first UDAN flight, on the Shimla-Delhi route, was flagged off by the Prime Minister on 27 April 2017.

fact_checks.claim: UDAN launched 21 October 2016 by the Ministry of Civil Aviation; first flight Shimla-Delhi on 27 April 2017

questions.subject: General Awareness and Current Affairs
questions.question_text: Which agency is the lead implementing agency of the National Agriculture Market (e-NAM)?

solution.explanation: e-NAM, an online trading platform linking APMC mandis, was launched by the Prime Minister on 14 April 2016 in 21 mandis of 8 States. It is fully funded by the Centre and implemented by SFAC under the Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare.
solution.final_answer: Option D: Small Farmers' Agribusiness Consortium (SFAC)

fact_checks.claim: e-NAM launched 14 April 2016; SFAC is the Lead Implementing Agency under the Ministry of Agriculture

questions.subject: General Awareness and Current Affairs
questions.question_text: PM-JANMAN, launched on Janjatiya Gaurav Divas (15 November 2023) at Khunti, Jharkhand, targets which group?

solution.explanation: Pradhan Mantri Janjati Adivasi Nyaya Maha Abhiyan (PM-JANMAN) aims to give PVTG households and habitations basic facilities such as housing, drinking water, roads, electricity, health and education. It covers 75 PVTG communities and is coordinated by the Ministry of Tribal Affairs with 9 ministries.
solution.final_answer: Option A: Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Groups (PVTGs)

fact_checks.claim: PM-JANMAN launched 15 Nov 2023 (Janjatiya Gaurav Divas) at Khunti for Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Groups

questions.subject: General Awareness and Current Affairs
questions.question_text: What was the total approved outlay of the Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY) for FY 2020-21 to FY 2024-25?

solution.explanation: PMMSY, the fisheries flagship of the Department of Fisheries, was approved by the Cabinet in May 2020 with an outlay of ₹20,050 crore (Centre ₹9,407 crore, States ₹4,880 crore, beneficiaries ₹5,763 crore) and launched on 10 September 2020. It has since been extended to 2025-26.
solution.why_others_wrong: ₹1 lakh crore is the size of the Agriculture Infrastructure Fund.

fact_checks.claim: PMMSY: total outlay ₹20,050 crore over five years FY 2020-21 to 2024-25

questions.subject: General Awareness and Current Affairs
questions.question_text: Under the Agriculture Infrastructure Fund, what rate of interest subvention is given on loans for post-harvest management infrastructure?

solution.explanation: The ₹1 lakh crore Agriculture Infrastructure Fund (launched by the PM on 9 August 2020) gives 3% per annum interest subvention and credit guarantee cover under CGTMSE on loans of up to ₹2 crore for post-harvest management infrastructure and community farming assets. The scheme runs from FY2020 to FY2029.
steps: Credit guarantee for loans up to ₹2 crore
solution.why_others_wrong: 1.5% is the interest subvention to lenders under the Modified Interest Subvention Scheme for KCC loans.

fact_checks.claim: AIF ₹1 lakh crore; interest subvention 3% per annum; CGTMSE guarantee for loans up to ₹2 crore

questions.subject: General Awareness and Current Affairs
questions.question_text: PM POSHAN, approved in September 2021, was earlier known by which name?

options.text: National Programme for Mid-Day Meal in Schools

solution.explanation: The Cabinet approved Pradhan Mantri Poshan Shakti Nirman (PM POSHAN) on 29 September 2021 as a modified version of the Mid-Day Meal scheme, for 2021-22 to 2025-26. It gives a hot cooked meal to children of Classes I-VIII in government and government-aided schools and adds pre-primary (Balvatika). The Ministry of Education runs it.
steps: PM POSHAN = renamed Mid-Day Meal scheme
solution.why_others_wrong: ICDS and POSHAN Abhiyaan are Ministry of Women and Child Development programmes.
solution.final_answer: Option D: National Programme for Mid-Day Meal in Schools

fact_checks.claim: PM POSHAN earlier known as National Programme for Mid-Day Meal in Schools; approved 29 Sept 2021; Classes I-VIII plus Balvatika

questions.subject: General Awareness and Current Affairs
questions.question_text:
Consider the following statements about the Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana (PMJDY):
1. It is described as the National Mission for Financial Inclusion.
2. The RuPay debit card issued to accounts opened after 28 August 2018 carries accident insurance cover of ₹2 lakh.
3. Account holders can avail an overdraft facility of up to ₹25,000.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

solution.explanation: PMJDY, the National Mission for Financial Inclusion, gives a basic savings account, a free RuPay card with accident cover of ₹2 lakh (₹1 lakh for accounts opened before 28 August 2018) and an overdraft facility of up to ₹10,000, not ₹25,000.
steps: Statement 3: wrong, the overdraft limit is ₹10,000

fact_checks.claim: PMJDY National Mission for Financial Inclusion; overdraft up to ₹10,000; RuPay accident cover ₹2 lakh (₹1 lakh before 28.8.2018)

questions.subject: General Awareness and Current Affairs
questions.question_text:
Consider the following statements about the Unified Pension Scheme (UPS) for Central Government employees:
1. The assured pension is 50% of the average basic pay of the last 12 months before superannuation, for a minimum qualifying service of 25 years.
2. The assured family pension is 60% of the employee's pension.
3. A minimum assured pension of ₹10,000 a month is paid on superannuation after at least 10 years of service.
4. The scheme came into effect from 1 April 2024.
Which of the statements given above are correct?

solution.explanation: The Cabinet approved UPS on 24 August 2024 as an option under the NPS for Central Government employees. It assures 50% of the average basic pay of the last 12 months (25 years' service, proportionate down to 10 years), 60% family pension and a minimum pension of ₹10,000 a month. It took effect from 1 April 2025, not 2024.
steps: Statements 1, 2 and 3 match the Cabinet decision

fact_checks.claim: UPS: 50% of average basic pay of last 12 months for 25 years service; family pension 60%; minimum ₹10,000 after 10 years; effective 1 April 2025

questions.subject: General Awareness and Current Affairs
questions.question_text: Under PM-KUSUM, implemented by the Ministry of New and Renewable Energy, what does Component-B provide for?

options.text: Installation of standalone solar-powered agricultural pumps
Decentralised ground-mounted grid-connected solar plants of up to 2 MW each
Solarisation of existing grid-connected agricultural pumps, including feeder-level solarisation
Rooftop solar plants on rural houses with up to 300 units of free electricity

solution.explanation: PM-KUSUM, approved by the CCEA on 19 February 2019, has three components: A, decentralised grid-connected renewable plants of up to 2 MW each; B, standalone (off-grid) solar agricultural pumps; and C, solarisation of grid-connected agricultural pumps, including feeder-level solarisation.
steps: Component A: small grid-connected plants (up to 2 MW)
solution.why_others_wrong: Rooftop solar with 300 free units is PM Surya Ghar, not PM-KUSUM.
solution.final_answer: Option A: Installation of standalone solar-powered agricultural pumps

fact_checks.claim: PM-KUSUM approved 19.2.2019 with Components A (plants up to 2 MW), B (standalone solar pumps) and C (solarisation of grid-connected pumps)

questions.subject: General Awareness and Current Affairs
questions.question_text:
Consider the following statements about the Kisan Credit Card (KCC):
1. The KCC scheme was introduced in 1998.
2. Under the Modified Interest Subvention Scheme, farmers get short-term KCC loans at 7%, which falls to an effective 4% with the 3% prompt repayment incentive.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

solution.explanation: The KCC scheme was introduced in 1998 so that farmers could buy inputs and draw cash for production needs. Under the Modified Interest Subvention Scheme, short-term crop loans through KCC carry 7% interest (lenders get 1.5% subvention), and prompt repayment earns a further 3% incentive, bringing the effective rate to 4%.

fact_checks.claim: KCC introduced in 1998; MISS: 7% interest, 1.5% subvention to lenders, 3% PRI, effective 4%

questions.subject: General Awareness and Current Affairs
questions.question_text:
Consider the following statements about Ayushman Bharat PM-JAY:
1. It was launched by the Prime Minister at Ranchi, Jharkhand, on 23 September 2018.
2. It covers only primary and outpatient care.
3. It is implemented by the National Health Authority.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

solution.explanation: PM-JAY was launched at Ranchi on 23 September 2018 and is run by the National Health Authority. It covers secondary and tertiary care hospitalisation (not primary/OPD care) of up to ₹5 lakh per family per year. Primary care is delivered through the Ayushman Arogya Mandirs (Health and Wellness Centres), the other pillar of Ayushman Bharat.
steps: 2: wrong, PM-JAY covers secondary and tertiary hospitalisation

fact_checks.claim: PM launched AB-PMJAY at Ranchi on 23 September 2018
PM-JAY covers secondary and tertiary hospitalisation; run by the National Health Authority

questions.subject: General Awareness and Current Affairs
questions.question_text:
Consider the following statements about the Smart Cities Mission:
1. It was launched on 25 June 2015.
2. It covers 100 cities.
3. It is implemented by the Ministry of Rural Development.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

solution.explanation: The Smart Cities Mission was launched by the Prime Minister on 25 June 2015, the same day as AMRUT, for 100 cities with central assistance of ₹48,000 crore. Being an urban mission, it is run by the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs, not the Ministry of Rural Development.

fact_checks.claim: Smart Cities Mission launched 25 June 2015 for 100 cities (MoHUA)

questions.subject: General Awareness and Current Affairs
questions.question_text:
Consider the following statements about the Prime Minister's Employment Generation Programme (PMEGP):
1. The Khadi and Village Industries Commission (KVIC) is its nodal agency at the national level.
2. It is a credit-linked subsidy programme for micro enterprises in the farm sector only.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

solution.explanation: PMEGP, run by the Ministry of MSME since 2008-09, is a credit-linked subsidy programme for self-employment through micro enterprises in the non-farm sector. KVIC is the national nodal agency; at State level KVIC offices, KVIBs, the Coir Board and District Industries Centres implement it.
steps: 2: wrong, it is for the non-farm sector

fact_checks.claim: PMEGP since 2008-09 for self-employment in the non-farm sector through banks; KVIC nodal agency

questions.subject: General Awareness and Current Affairs
questions.question_text:
Consider the following statements:
1. The PM GatiShakti National Master Plan was launched on 13 October 2021.
2. The National Logistics Policy was launched before the PM GatiShakti National Master Plan.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

solution.concept: PM GatiShakti and National Logistics Policy
solution.explanation: The PM GatiShakti National Master Plan, a GIS-based platform for integrated multimodal infrastructure planning, was launched on 13 October 2021. The National Logistics Policy came later, on 17 September 2022, to deal with the 'soft' side (processes, skills, digital systems) through the Comprehensive Logistics Action Plan.

fact_checks.claim: PM GatiShakti NMP launched 13 October 2021; National Logistics Policy launched 17 September 2022

questions.subject: General Awareness and Current Affairs
questions.question_text:
Consider the following statements about the Jal Jeevan Mission:
1. It was announced by the Prime Minister on 15 August 2019.
2. When it began, only about 3.23 crore (about 17%) rural households had tap water connections.
3. The mission has been extended up to 2028.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

solution.explanation: JJM was announced from the Red Fort on 15 August 2019 with the goal of tap water for every rural household by 2024. At the start only 3.23 crore households (16.71%) had tap connections; the mission has since been extended to 2028.

fact_checks.claim: JJM launched 15 Aug 2019; at launch 3.23 crore households (16.71%) had tap water; extended to 2028

questions.subject: General Awareness and Current Affairs
questions.question_text:
Consider the following statements about PM SVANidhi:
1. It was launched by the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs on 1 June 2020.
2. It is a joint responsibility of the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs and the Department of Financial Services.
3. Loans under the scheme require collateral security.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

solution.explanation: PM SVANidhi was launched by MoHUA on 1 June 2020 and is run jointly with the Department of Financial Services. Its working-capital loans are collateral-free, with an interest subsidy and cashback on digital transactions. Lending has been extended to March 2030.

fact_checks.claim: PM SVANidhi launched by MoHUA 1 June 2020; joint responsibility of MoHUA and DFS; collateral-free loans

questions.subject: General Awareness and Current Affairs

solution.explanation: The World Economic Forum introduced the Global Gender Gap Index in 2006 and publishes it every year. It measures gaps between women and men in four areas.
solution.why_others_wrong: UNDP publishes the Gender Development Index and Gender Inequality Index in its Human Development Report.

fact_checks.claim: WEF first introduced the Global Gender Gap Index in 2006; published annually

questions.subject: General Awareness and Current Affairs
questions.question_text: The Human Development Report, which contains the Human Development Index, is published by:

solution.explanation: The HDR is published by UNDP's Human Development Report Office. The HDI combines life expectancy, education (expected and mean years of schooling) and GNI per capita.
solution.final_answer: Option C: United Nations Development Programme (UNDP)

fact_checks.claim: UNDP's Human Development Report ranks countries on HDI

questions.subject: General Awareness and Current Affairs
questions.question_text: The Global Innovation Index is published by which organisation?

solution.explanation: WIPO, the UN agency for intellectual property based in Geneva, publishes the Global Innovation Index every year. It ranks about 140 economies on innovation inputs and outputs using about 80 indicators.
solution.final_answer: Option A: World Intellectual Property Organization (WIPO)

fact_checks.claim: India ranking in the Global Innovation Index 2025, published by WIPO

questions.subject: General Awareness and Current Affairs
questions.question_text: The World Investment Report, which tracks global foreign direct investment, is published by:

solution.explanation: The World Investment Report is UNCTAD's annual flagship on FDI trends and investment policy. UNCTAD (UN Trade and Development) is headquartered in Geneva.

fact_checks.claim: World Investment Report 2026 published by UNCTAD

questions.subject: General Awareness and Current Affairs
questions.question_text: The 'Global Economic Prospects' report, released every January and June, is published by:

solution.explanation: Global Economic Prospects is a World Bank flagship report published twice a year (January and June), with a special focus on emerging market and developing economies.
solution.why_others_wrong: The IMF publishes the World Economic Outlook (April and October).

fact_checks.claim: Global Economic Prospects is a semiannual (January and June) World Bank flagship report

questions.subject: General Awareness and Current Affairs
questions.question_text: In India, the Financial Stability Report is published by:

options.text: Securities and Exchange Board of India

solution.explanation: The RBI publishes the Financial Stability Report. It draws contributions from all financial sector regulators and assesses risks to the stability of the Indian financial system.
solution.final_answer: Option B: Reserve Bank of India

fact_checks.claim: The FSR is published by the RBI

questions.subject: General Awareness and Current Affairs
questions.question_text: The Global Hunger Index is jointly published by which organisations?

solution.explanation: The GHI is a peer-reviewed annual report co-published by Welthungerhilfe (Bonn) and Concern Worldwide (Dublin). It scores countries on undernourishment, child stunting, child wasting and child mortality.
solution.why_others_wrong: FAO, IFAD, UNICEF, WFP and WHO jointly publish a different report, SOFI.
solution.final_answer: Option A: Welthungerhilfe and Concern Worldwide

fact_checks.claim: GHI published by Welthungerhilfe (Bonn) and Concern Worldwide (Dublin)

questions.subject: General Awareness and Current Affairs
questions.question_text: The World Happiness Report is published by the Wellbeing Research Centre of which university, in partnership with Gallup and the UN Sustainable Development Solutions Network?

solution.explanation: The annual World Happiness Report is published by the University of Oxford's Wellbeing Research Centre in partnership with Gallup, the UN Sustainable Development Solutions Network and an editorial board. Its main data source is the Gallup World Poll.

fact_checks.claim: WHR published by the University of Oxford's Wellbeing Research Centre with Gallup and UN SDSN

questions.subject: General Awareness and Current Affairs
questions.question_text: The Global Peace Index is published by which organisation?

solution.explanation: The Institute for Economics & Peace (IEP), a Sydney-headquartered think tank, publishes the Global Peace Index, the Global Terrorism Index and the Positive Peace Report.
steps: IEP also publishes the Global Terrorism Index
solution.why_others_wrong: SIPRI is known for its military expenditure and arms transfer databases.
solution.final_answer: Option A: Institute for Economics & Peace

fact_checks.claim: IEP develops the Global Peace Index, Global Terrorism Index and Positive Peace

questions.subject: General Awareness and Current Affairs
questions.question_text: The World Competitiveness Ranking is published by:

solution.explanation: The IMD World Competitiveness Center at IMD business school in Lausanne, Switzerland, publishes the World Competitiveness Ranking (yearbook since 1989), along with the World Digital Competitiveness and World Talent rankings.
solution.why_others_wrong: The WEF published the Global Competitiveness Report, a different report.
solution.final_answer: Option C: IMD World Competitiveness Center, Lausanne

fact_checks.claim: World Competitiveness Ranking by IMD World Competitiveness Center

questions.subject: General Awareness and Current Affairs
questions.question_text: The Environmental Performance Index is produced jointly by:

solution.explanation: The EPI is produced by the Yale Center for Environmental Law & Policy and the Center for International Earth Science Information Network (CIESIN) at Columbia University. It ranks countries on environmental health, ecosystem vitality and climate change.
solution.final_answer: Option B: Yale University and Columbia University

fact_checks.claim: EPI is run by the Yale Center for Environmental Law & Policy and CIESIN at Columbia University

questions.subject: General Awareness and Current Affairs
questions.question_text: The Global Multidimensional Poverty Index is published jointly by UNDP and:

options.text: Oxford Poverty and Human Development Initiative (OPHI)

solution.explanation: The global MPI was developed by OPHI (University of Oxford) with UNDP for the 2010 Human Development Report and has been published annually since. A person is 'MPI poor' if deprived in a third or more of ten weighted indicators across health, education and living standards.
solution.final_answer: Option D: Oxford Poverty and Human Development Initiative (OPHI)

fact_checks.claim: Global MPI developed by OPHI with UNDP in 2010 and published annually; ten weighted indicators

questions.subject: General Awareness and Current Affairs
questions.question_text: In the World Bank's Logistics Performance Index 2023, what was India's rank out of 139 countries?

solution.explanation: India ranked 38th of 139 countries in the World Bank's LPI 2023, up six places from 44th in 2018 (and from 54th in 2014). The government credits PM GatiShakti and the National Logistics Policy.

fact_checks.claim: India ranks 38 of 139 in LPI 2023; improved from 44 (2018) and 54 (2014)

questions.subject: General Awareness and Current Affairs
questions.question_text: In UNDP's Human Development Report 2025, what was India's HDI rank out of 193 countries?

solution.explanation: India ranked 130th of 193 countries in the HDR 2025 with an HDI value of 0.685 (for 2023), in the medium human development category. Inequality reduces India's HDI by 30.7%.
solution.why_others_wrong: 134 was India's rank in the 2023-24 report.

fact_checks.claim: India ranks 130 out of 193 countries in the 2025 HDR; HDI 0.685

questions.subject: General Awareness and Current Affairs
questions.question_text: What was India's rank in WIPO's Global Innovation Index 2025?

solution.explanation: India ranked 38th in the GII 2025, its best so far, up from 66th in 2019 and 81st in 2015. It ranks first in the Central and Southern Asia region.

fact_checks.claim: India's GII rank improved to 38th in 2025 from 66th in 2019

questions.subject: General Awareness and Current Affairs
questions.question_text: The 'State of World Population' report is the annual flagship publication of which body?

options.text: UN Department of Economic and Social Affairs

solution.explanation: The State of World Population report is UNFPA's annual flagship. Each edition takes up a population or sexual and reproductive health theme; the 2025 edition was titled 'The real fertility crisis'.
solution.why_others_wrong: UN DESA publishes 'World Population Prospects', a different report.
solution.final_answer: Option B: United Nations Population Fund (UNFPA)

fact_checks.claim: State of World Population 2025 published by UNFPA

questions.subject: General Awareness and Current Affairs
questions.question_text:
Consider the following statements about the Global Hunger Index (GHI):
1. It is based on four indicators: undernourishment, child stunting, child wasting and child mortality.
2. All four indicators carry equal weight in the GHI score.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

solution.explanation: The GHI combines four indicators. Undernourishment and child mortality each contribute one-third of the score, while child stunting and child wasting each contribute one-sixth, so the weights are not equal.

fact_checks.claim: GHI: undernourishment and child mortality one-third each; stunting and wasting one-sixth each

questions.subject: General Awareness and Current Affairs
questions.question_text: In the RBI's Financial Inclusion Index (FI-Index), which of the three sub-indices carries the highest weight?

solution.explanation: The RBI's FI-Index (0 to 100) has three sub-indices: Access (35%), Usage (45%) and Quality (20%), built from 97 indicators. It is published annually; the index for March 2025 was 67.0.
steps: So Usage has the highest weight

fact_checks.claim: FI-Index sub-indices Access 35%, Usage 45%, Quality 20%; 97 indicators

questions.subject: General Awareness and Current Affairs
questions.question_text:
Consider the following statements about the RBI's Financial Stability Report (FSR):
1. It is a half-yearly publication.
2. It presents the collective assessment of the Sub-Committee of the Financial Stability and Development Council (FSDC).
3. It is published by the Ministry of Finance.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

solution.explanation: The FSR is a half-yearly RBI publication (June and December) with contributions from all financial sector regulators. It reflects the collective assessment of the Sub-Committee of the FSDC (chaired by the RBI Governor) on risks to financial stability.
steps: 3: wrong, it is an RBI publication

fact_checks.claim: FSR is a half-yearly publication presenting the collective assessment of the Sub Committee of the FSDC

questions.subject: General Awareness and Current Affairs
questions.question_text:
Consider the following statements about the World Happiness Report:
1. Country rankings are based on life evaluations on the Cantril ladder (0 to 10) from the Gallup World Poll.
2. The ranking score is a composite index that adds up weighted values of GDP, life expectancy and other metrics.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

solution.explanation: Rankings use people's own answers on the Cantril ladder (0 = worst possible life, 10 = best), averaged over three years. GDP per capita, social support and other factors are used only to explain the differences; the report does not build a composite index.
steps: 2: wrong, the ranking is not a composite index

fact_checks.claim: Rankings based on Cantril ladder from the Gallup World Poll rather than an index from multiple metrics

questions.subject: General Awareness and Current Affairs
questions.question_text:
Consider the following statements about the World Press Freedom Index:
1. It has been published every year since 2002.
2. It ranks 180 countries and territories.
3. It measures the quality of journalism in each country.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

solution.explanation: RSF's Index, published every year since 2002, ranks 180 countries and territories on political, economic, legal, social and security indicators. It measures the conditions for press freedom, not the quality of journalism.

fact_checks.claim: Published every year since 2002; 180 countries; not a measure of journalism quality

questions.subject: General Awareness and Current Affairs
questions.question_text: In NITI Aayog's SDG India Index 2023-24 (the fourth edition), what was India's overall composite score?

solution.explanation: The SDG India Index 2023-24, released on 12 July 2024, gave India a composite score of 71, up from 66 in 2020-21 and 57 in the 2018 baseline. It tracks States and UTs on 113 indicators aligned to MoSPI's National Indicator Framework. Goal 13 (Climate Action) improved the most.

fact_checks.claim: Overall SDG score 71 for 2023-24, up from 66 (2020-21) and 57 (2018); 113 indicators

questions.subject: General Awareness and Current Affairs
questions.question_text: Which of the following is NOT one of the four subindexes of the Global Gender Gap Index?

solution.explanation: The Global Gender Gap Index has four subindexes: Economic Participation and Opportunity, Educational Attainment, Health and Survival, and Political Empowerment. Political Empowerment has the largest remaining gap.
steps: Four subindexes: economic, education, health, political
Digital access is not one of them

fact_checks.claim: GGGI subindexes: Economic Participation and Opportunity, Educational Attainment, Health and Survival, Political Empowerment

questions.subject: General Awareness and Current Affairs
questions.question_text:
Consider the following statements about India in the Global Innovation Index (GII):
1. India was ranked 66th in 2019.
2. In 2025 India topped the lower middle-income group of economies.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

solution.explanation: The Economic Survey 2025-26 notes that India's GII rank rose from 66th in 2019 to 38th in 2025. This places India at the top of the lower middle-income group and first in Central and Southern Asia.

fact_checks.claim: GII rank improved from 66th in 2019 to 38th in 2025; top of lower middle-income group

questions.subject: General Awareness and Current Affairs
questions.question_text: The Goods and Services Tax (GST) was rolled out in India from which date?

solution.explanation: GST was rolled out at midnight on 30 June-1 July 2017 at a ceremony in the Central Hall of Parliament. It replaced many central and state taxes such as excise duty, service tax, VAT and entry tax. 1 July is observed as GST Day.

fact_checks.claim: GST rolled out on the midnight of 1 July 2017 in the Central Hall of Parliament

questions.subject: General Awareness and Current Affairs
questions.question_text: Who chairs the GST Council?

solution.explanation: Under Article 279A, the GST Council is a joint forum of the Centre and the States. The Union Finance Minister is its Chairperson; the Union Minister of State for Revenue and the Finance or Taxation Ministers of the States are members.

fact_checks.claim: GST Council under Article 279A: Union Finance Minister as Chairperson, MoS Revenue and State Finance Ministers as members

questions.subject: General Awareness and Current Affairs
questions.question_text: The Income-tax Act, 2025, which came into force on 1 April 2026, replaced which law?

solution.explanation: The Income-tax Act, 2025 was passed by Parliament on 12 August 2025, received assent on 21 August 2025 and came into force on 1 April 2026, replacing the Income-tax Act, 1961. It simplifies language and roughly halves the word count, without major rate changes.

fact_checks.claim: Income-tax Act, 2025 came into force on 1 April 2026, replacing the Income-tax Act, 1961

questions.subject: General Awareness and Current Affairs
questions.question_text: Under the National Education Policy 2020, the 10+2 school structure is replaced by which structure?

solution.explanation: NEP 2020, approved on 29 July 2020, replaces the 10+2 structure with 5+3+3+4, covering ages 3-8 (foundational), 8-11 (preparatory), 11-14 (middle) and 14-18 (secondary). This brings ages 3-6 into the school curriculum for the first time.
solution.shortcut: Add the years: 5+3+3+4 = 15 years, from age 3 to 18.

fact_checks.claim: 10+2 replaced by 5+3+3+4 corresponding to ages 3-8, 8-11, 11-14 and 14-18

questions.subject: General Awareness and Current Affairs
questions.question_text: How many Labour Codes did the Government of India make effective from 21 November 2025, consolidating 29 central labour laws?

solution.explanation: From 21 November 2025 the Government made four Labour Codes effective: the Code on Wages, 2019; the Industrial Relations Code, 2020; the Code on Social Security, 2020; and the Occupational Safety, Health and Working Conditions Code, 2020. Together they replace 29 central labour laws.

fact_checks.claim: Four Labour Codes effective 21 November 2025, consolidating 29 Central labour laws

questions.subject: General Awareness and Current Affairs
questions.question_text: Under the GST rate rationalisation effective from 22 September 2025, what are the two main GST rates?

solution.explanation: On the recommendation of the 56th GST Council meeting (3 September 2025), the four-slab structure (5, 12, 18, 28%) was replaced from 22 September 2025 by two main rates, 5% (merit) and 18% (standard), plus a special 40% rate for a few sin and luxury goods.

fact_checks.claim: 56th GST Council: two main rates 5% and 18% plus special 40%; effective 22 September 2025

questions.subject: General Awareness and Current Affairs
questions.question_text: After the GST changes effective 22 September 2025, what is the special GST rate applied to a few sin and luxury goods, such as cars above 1500 cc?

solution.explanation: The special 40% rate covers a few sin and luxury goods, such as mid-size and large cars (above 1500 cc or longer than 4000 mm) and motorcycles above 350 cc. Most of these goods earlier carried 28% GST plus compensation cess; the cess was merged into the GST rate as the cess is being ended.
steps: Example: cars above 1500 cc, motorcycles above 350 cc
solution.why_others_wrong: 28% was the highest regular slab before the reform.

fact_checks.claim: Special 40% rate on few sin and luxury goods; cars above 1500 cc or 4000 mm at 40%; motorcycles above 350 cc at 40%

questions.subject: General Awareness and Current Affairs
questions.question_text: The Income-tax Act, 2025 replaces the concepts of 'Previous Year' and 'Assessment Year' with which single concept?

solution.explanation: The new Act uses one term, 'Tax Year', defined as the twelve-month financial year starting on 1 April, in place of the old pair of 'Previous Year' (when income is earned) and 'Assessment Year' (when it is assessed).

fact_checks.claim: Income-tax Act 2025 replaces 'Assessment Year' and 'Previous Year' with a single 'Tax Year'

questions.subject: General Awareness and Current Affairs
questions.question_text: The Jan Vishwas (Amendment of Provisions) Act, 2023 decriminalised 183 provisions in how many Central Acts?

solution.explanation: The Jan Vishwas Act, 2023 decriminalised 183 provisions in 42 Central Acts administered by 19 ministries and departments, replacing many imprisonment clauses for minor and technical offences with monetary penalties to improve ease of living and doing business.
solution.why_others_wrong: 19 is the number of ministries/departments and 183 the number of provisions.

fact_checks.claim: Jan Vishwas Act 2023 decriminalized 183 provisions under 42 Acts administered by 19 Ministries/Departments

questions.subject: General Awareness and Current Affairs
questions.question_text: Under the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016, the corporate insolvency resolution process must be completed within an outer limit of how many days, including extensions and litigation time?

solution.explanation: The CIRP must normally finish within 180 days of admission, extendable once by up to 90 days with a 66% vote of the committee of creditors. A 2019 amendment set an overall cap of 330 days that includes extensions and time taken in legal proceedings. If no resolution plan is approved, the corporate debtor goes into liquidation.
solution.why_others_wrong: 270 days = 180 + 90, without litigation time.

fact_checks.claim: CIRP 180 days, one extension up to 90 days, overall 330 days including legal proceedings

questions.subject: General Awareness and Current Affairs
questions.question_text: India's Foreign Trade Policy 2023 came into effect on which date?

solution.explanation: The Foreign Trade Policy 2023 was launched on 31 March 2023 and came into effect on 1 April 2023. Unlike earlier five-year policies, it has no fixed end date and is updated as needed. It is administered by the DGFT under the Ministry of Commerce and Industry.

fact_checks.claim: FTP 2023 launched on 31 March 2023 and came into effect from 1 April 2023

questions.subject: General Awareness and Current Affairs
questions.question_text: Under the corporate tax cuts of September 2019, what is the base income-tax rate for new domestic manufacturing companies incorporated on or after 1 October 2019 that claim no exemptions?

solution.explanation: The Taxation Laws (Amendment) Ordinance, 2019 let existing domestic companies pay 22% (effective 25.17% with surcharge and cess) and new domestic manufacturing companies incorporated on or after 1 October 2019 pay 15% (effective 17.01%), if they give up exemptions and incentives.
solution.why_others_wrong: 22% is the rate for existing domestic companies; 17% is close to the effective rate including surcharge and cess.

fact_checks.claim: 15% for new domestic manufacturing companies incorporated on or after 1 October 2019; 22% for existing domestic companies

questions.subject: General Awareness and Current Affairs
questions.question_text:
Consider the following statements about GST:
1. It was introduced through the Constitution (101st Amendment) Act, 2016.
2. The GST Council is constituted under Article 279A of the Constitution.
3. At its launch in 2017, GST had a single uniform rate of 18%.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

solution.explanation: GST was enabled by the Constitution (101st Amendment) Act, 2016 (the 122nd Amendment Bill), which inserted Article 279A for the GST Council. At launch GST had four main slabs of 5%, 12%, 18% and 28%, not a single rate.

fact_checks.claim: Constitution (101st Amendment) Act 2016; Article 279A GST Council; four-slab structure 5, 12, 18, 28%

questions.subject: General Awareness and Current Affairs
questions.question_text:
Consider the following statements about the Labour Codes made effective in November 2025:
1. Fixed-term employees become eligible for gratuity after one year of service instead of five.
2. ESIC coverage is mandatory for establishments with more than 10 employees.
3. The four codes together replace 44 central labour laws.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

solution.explanation: The Labour Codes reduce the gratuity eligibility period for fixed-term employees to one year, extend ESIC coverage on a mandatory basis to establishments with more than 10 employees and give every worker a statutory right to minimum wages. They consolidate 29 central labour laws, not 44.

fact_checks.claim: Labour Codes: gratuity after one year for fixed-term employees; ESIC mandatory for more than 10 employees; 29 central laws

questions.subject: General Awareness and Current Affairs
questions.question_text:
Consider the following statements about India's data protection framework:
1. The Digital Personal Data Protection Rules, 2025 were notified in November 2025 to operationalise the DPDP Act, 2023.
2. Appeals against decisions of the Data Protection Board of India lie with the TDSAT.
3. The highest penalty, up to ₹250 crore, applies to a Data Fiduciary's failure to maintain reasonable security safeguards.
4. The Rules give organisations a phased compliance period of 36 months.
Which of the statements given above are correct?

solution.explanation: The DPDP Rules, 2025 were notified in November 2025, fully operationalising the DPDP Act, 2023. They set up a fully digital Data Protection Board; appeals go to TDSAT. The highest penalty (up to ₹250 crore) is for failing to maintain reasonable security safeguards. The phased compliance timeline is 18 months, not 36.

fact_checks.claim: DPDP Rules 2025 notified; Data Protection Board; appeals to TDSAT; 18-month phased compliance; penalty up to ₹250 crore for security safeguards failure

questions.subject: General Awareness and Current Affairs
questions.question_text:
Consider the following statements about the National Education Policy 2020:
1. It was approved by the Union Cabinet on 29 July 2020.
2. It replaced the National Policy on Education, 1986.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

solution.explanation: The Union Cabinet approved NEP 2020 on 29 July 2020. It replaced the 34-year-old National Policy on Education, 1986, and is the first education policy of the 21st century.

fact_checks.claim: NEP 2020 approved 29 July 2020; replaces the National Policy on Education, 1986

questions.subject: General Awareness and Current Affairs
questions.question_text:
Consider the following statements about the corporate tax reform of September 2019:
1. Domestic companies opting for the 22% rate have an effective tax rate of 25.17%, including surcharge and cess.
2. Companies opting for the 22% rate are exempt from Minimum Alternate Tax (MAT).
3. The 22% option is available only to companies incorporated on or after 1 October 2019.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

solution.explanation: Any domestic company that gives up exemptions and incentives can opt for 22% (effective 25.17%) and is then not required to pay MAT. The 1 October 2019 incorporation condition applies only to the separate 15% option for new manufacturing companies.
steps: 3: wrong, that condition is for the 15% option

fact_checks.claim: 22% option for domestic companies, effective 25.17%, not required to pay MAT; 15% for new manufacturing companies incorporated on or after 1 Oct 2019

questions.subject: General Awareness and Current Affairs
questions.question_text: What is the currency of Bhutan?

solution.explanation: Bhutan's currency is the ngultrum (BTN), pegged at par with the Indian rupee. Its capital is Thimphu.
solution.why_others_wrong: Taka: Bangladesh; Kyat: Myanmar; Rufiyaa: Maldives.

fact_checks.claim: Bhutan: capital Thimphu; currency ngultrum (BTN)

questions.subject: General Awareness and Current Affairs
questions.question_text: What is the capital of Kazakhstan?

solution.explanation: Kazakhstan's capital is Astana; its currency is the tenge. Almaty is its largest city and former capital.
solution.why_others_wrong: Tashkent is the capital of Uzbekistan and Bishkek of Kyrgyzstan.

fact_checks.claim: Kazakhstan: capital Astana; currency tenge (KZT)

questions.subject: General Awareness and Current Affairs
questions.question_text: What is the capital of Vietnam?

solution.explanation: Vietnam's capital is Hanoi; its currency is the dong. Ho Chi Minh City (formerly Saigon) is its largest city.

fact_checks.claim: Vietnam: capital Hanoi (Ha Noi)

questions.subject: General Awareness and Current Affairs
questions.question_text: Kaziranga National Park, famous for the one-horned rhinoceros, is in which state?

solution.explanation: Kaziranga National Park in Assam was inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1985. It holds the world's largest population of the greater one-horned rhinoceros.

fact_checks.claim: Kaziranga National Park, Assam, inscribed 1985; largest population of Indian one-horned rhino

questions.subject: General Awareness and Current Affairs
questions.question_text: The Gir landscape of Gujarat is the only wild home of which animal?

solution.explanation: The Asiatic lion survives in the wild only in the Gir landscape of Gujarat. The population rose from 674 in 2020 to 891 in 2025; the census is held every five years.
steps: Asiatic lion: only in Gir landscape, Gujarat

fact_checks.claim: Asiatic lion population in Gir landscape rose from 674 (2020) to 891 (2025)

questions.subject: General Awareness and Current Affairs
questions.question_text: The Tehri Dam in Uttarakhand is built on which river?

solution.explanation: Tehri Dam is a 260.5 m earth and rockfill dam on the Bhagirathi, just downstream of its confluence with the Bhilangana, in Uttarakhand. THDC India Ltd operates it.

fact_checks.claim: Tehri: 260.5 m earth and rockfill dam across River Bhagirathi; THDC

questions.subject: General Awareness and Current Affairs
questions.question_text: In which year did Telangana come into existence as a separate state?

solution.explanation: Telangana, India's youngest state, came into existence on 2 June 2014 under the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014. 2 June is Telangana Formation Day.
solution.why_others_wrong: 2000 saw the creation of Chhattisgarh, Uttarakhand and Jharkhand; in 2019 J&K was reorganised into UTs.

fact_checks.claim: Telangana, India's youngest State, came into existence on 2 June 2014

questions.subject: General Awareness and Current Affairs
questions.question_text: Which city is the administrative capital of Myanmar?

solution.explanation: Myanmar's administrative capital is Nay Pyi Taw; Yangon (Rangoon) was the earlier capital and is the largest city. Myanmar's currency is the kyat.
steps: Myanmar: administrative capital Nay Pyi Taw, currency kyat

fact_checks.claim: Burma: Nay Pyi Taw is the administrative capital; currency kyat (MMK)

questions.subject: General Awareness and Current Affairs
questions.question_text: Which city is the legislative capital of Sri Lanka?

solution.explanation: Sri Lanka has two capitals: Sri Jayewardenepura Kotte (legislative capital, seat of Parliament) and Colombo (commercial capital). Kotte's name means 'Resplendent City of Growing Victory'.

fact_checks.claim: Sri Lanka: Colombo (commercial capital); Sri Jayewardenepura Kotte (legislative capital)

questions.subject: General Awareness and Current Affairs
questions.question_text: What is the currency of the Maldives?

solution.explanation: The Maldives uses the rufiyaa (MVR); its capital is Male. Nepal, Pakistan and Sri Lanka use rupees, and Bhutan uses the ngultrum.

fact_checks.claim: Maldives currency: rufiyaa (MVR)

questions.subject: General Awareness and Current Affairs
questions.question_text: Keibul Lamjao, described as the only floating national park in the world, is located in which state?

solution.explanation: Keibul Lamjao lies on Loktak Lake in Manipur and is made of floating mats of vegetation called phumdis. It is the only natural home of the sangai (brow-antlered deer), Manipur's state animal.

fact_checks.claim: Keibul Lamjao on Loktak Lake, Manipur: sangai deer habitat on floating phumdis

questions.subject: General Awareness and Current Affairs
questions.question_text: Jim Corbett National Park was originally established in 1936 under which name?

solution.explanation: Corbett was established in 1936 as Hailey National Park, after Sir Malcolm Hailey, Governor of the United Provinces; it was the first national park of mainland Asia. It was briefly called Ramganga National Park (1954-55) and was renamed after Jim Corbett in 1956.
solution.why_others_wrong: Ramganga was a later, short-lived name, not the original one.

fact_checks.claim: Originally established as Hailey National Park in 1936; Ramganga NP 1954-55; renamed after Jim Corbett in 1956

questions.subject: General Awareness and Current Affairs
questions.question_text: In which year was the Sundarbans National Park (India) inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site?

solution.explanation: Sundarbans National Park in West Bengal, the world's largest mangrove delta and a tiger habitat, was inscribed in 1987. Kaziranga, Manas and Keoladeo were inscribed earlier, in 1985.

fact_checks.claim: Sundarbans National Park inscribed 1987 under criteria (ix) and (x)

questions.subject: General Awareness and Current Affairs
questions.question_text: The Hirakud Dam, near Sambalpur in Odisha, is built on which river?

solution.explanation: Hirakud Dam is on the Mahanadi about 15 km from Sambalpur, Odisha. It is often described as one of the longest earthen dams in the world, and its reservoir is among the largest artificial lakes in Asia.

fact_checks.claim: Hirakud Dam on the Mahanadi near Sambalpur

questions.subject: General Awareness and Current Affairs
questions.question_text: What is the name of the reservoir formed by the Bhakra Dam on the Sutlej?

solution.explanation: Bhakra Dam is a 225.55 m concrete gravity dam across the Sutlej in Bilaspur district, Himachal Pradesh. Its reservoir is Gobind Sagar. The Bhakra Beas Management Board (BBMB) operates it.
solution.why_others_wrong: Rana Pratap Sagar is on the Chambal; Govind Ballabh Pant Sagar (Rihand) is in Uttar Pradesh.

fact_checks.claim: Bhakra Dam on Sutlej, Bilaspur HP; reservoir Gobind Sagar; BBMB

questions.subject: General Awareness and Current Affairs
questions.question_text: Goa became which state of the Indian Union on 30 May 1987?

solution.explanation: Goa, administered as a Union Territory (with Daman and Diu) after its liberation in 1961, became the 25th state on 30 May 1987, celebrated as Goa Statehood Day.

fact_checks.claim: Goa became the 25th State of the Indian Union on 30 May 1987

questions.subject: General Awareness and Current Affairs
questions.question_text: On which date was Nagaland inaugurated as a state?

solution.explanation: Nagaland was formally inaugurated as the 16th state of India on 1 December 1963 under the State of Nagaland Act, 1962. The Hornbill Festival begins on Statehood Day, 1 December.
solution.why_others_wrong: 21 January 1972: Manipur, Meghalaya and Tripura; 20 February 1987: Arunachal Pradesh and Mizoram.

fact_checks.claim: Nagaland inaugurated 1 December 1963 as the 16th state of India

questions.subject: General Awareness and Current Affairs
questions.question_text:
Consider the following statements about South Africa:
1. Pretoria is its administrative capital.
2. Cape Town is its judicial capital.
3. Bloemfontein is its judicial capital.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

solution.concept: Countries with more than one capital
solution.explanation: South Africa has three capitals: Pretoria (administrative), Cape Town (legislative) and Bloemfontein (judicial). Its currency is the rand.

fact_checks.claim: South Africa: Pretoria administrative, Cape Town legislative, Bloemfontein judicial

questions.subject: General Awareness and Current Affairs
questions.question_text: The power from the Sardar Sarovar Project on the Narmada is shared among states under the Narmada tribunal award. Which state gets the largest share?

solution.explanation: Sardar Sarovar Dam at Kevadia (Narmada district, Gujarat) is an inter-state project of Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra, Gujarat and Rajasthan. Its 1,450 MW of power is shared 57% to Madhya Pradesh, 27% to Maharashtra and 16% to Gujarat; Rajasthan gets water but no power. The Statue of Unity stands near the dam.
solution.why_others_wrong: Gujarat hosts the dam and gets most of the water, but the smallest power share.

fact_checks.claim: SSP at Kevadia; interstate project of MP, Maharashtra, Gujarat, Rajasthan; power 57% MP, 27% Maharashtra, 16% Gujarat

questions.subject: General Awareness and Current Affairs
questions.question_text:
Consider the following statements about Jim Corbett National Park:
1. It was renamed after Jim Corbett in 1956.
2. Project Tiger was launched at Corbett on 1 April 1973.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

solution.explanation: The park was renamed in honour of Jim Corbett in 1956, after his death. Project Tiger was launched at the Corbett Tiger Reserve on 1 April 1973 (the Dhikala Forest Rest House was the venue), starting with nine tiger reserves.

fact_checks.claim: Renamed in honour of Jim Corbett in 1956; launch site of Project Tiger on 1 April 1973

questions.subject: General Awareness and Current Affairs
questions.question_text:
Consider the following statements:
1. Kaziranga National Park was inscribed as a World Heritage Site in 1985.
2. Keoladeo National Park was the only wintering ground in India of the Siberian crane.
3. Keoladeo National Park is located in Gujarat.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

solution.explanation: Kaziranga (Assam) and Keoladeo were both inscribed in 1985. Keoladeo National Park is at Bharatpur in Rajasthan, not Gujarat; it was the only wintering ground in India of the rare Siberian crane and is also a Ramsar wetland.

fact_checks.claim: Kaziranga National Park inscribed 1985
Keoladeo National Park, Bharatpur: only wintering ground in India of the Siberian crane
Keoladeo National Park inscribed 1985

questions.subject: General Awareness and Current Affairs
questions.question_text:
Consider the following statements about the reorganisation of Jammu and Kashmir:
1. The Union Territories of Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh came into existence on 31 October 2019.
2. The Union Territory of Ladakh has a legislature.
3. The Union Territory of Jammu and Kashmir has a legislature.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

solution.explanation: Under the Jammu and Kashmir Reorganisation Act, 2019, the state was split into the UT of Jammu and Kashmir (with a legislature) and the UT of Ladakh (without a legislature), with effect from 31 October 2019, the birth anniversary of Sardar Patel.

fact_checks.claim: UT of J&K with legislature and UT of Ladakh without legislature, in force from 31 October 2019

questions.subject: General Awareness and Current Affairs
questions.question_text:
Consider the following statements:
1. Gujarat and Maharashtra were formed on 1 May 1960 by dividing the former Bombay State.
2. Sikkim became a state of India on 16 May 1975.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

solution.explanation: On 1 May 1960 the bilingual Bombay State was divided into Gujarat and Maharashtra, and both observe 1 May as their Foundation Day. Sikkim became a state on 16 May 1975 (Constitution 36th Amendment); 2025 marked 50 years of its statehood.

fact_checks.claim: Gujarat carved out of the former Bombay State on 1 May 1960
Sikkim Statehood Day 16 May (1975)

questions.subject: General Awareness and Current Affairs
questions.question_text:
Consider the following statements about the Tehri Dam:
1. It is a 260.5 m high earth and rockfill dam.
2. It is owned and operated by NHPC Limited.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

solution.explanation: Tehri is a 260.5 m earth and rockfill dam with a 1,000 MW underground power house. It is owned and operated by THDC India Ltd, not NHPC. The Tehri complex also includes a 1,000 MW pumped storage plant.

fact_checks.claim: Tehri HPP: 260.5 m earth and rockfill dam; THDC India Ltd
